Below are the accuracy metrics reported by deepbiosphere along with explanations from the supplement of Gillespie et al. 2024. In the plots below I am showing the per-species metrics for the full species list and for bee floral resources. Significance comparisons are made between deepbiosphere and four other modeling approaches available in the deepbiosphere repository: BioclimMLP, a multilayer perceptron trained only on the Bioclim data; TResNet, a deep neural net model trained only on the NAIP imagery; Maxent, a maximum entropy modeling approach trained on bioclimatic data; and a random forest model trained on bioclimatic data.

title: Accuracy metrics – uniform train-test
text:
Binary classification metrics
These metrics threshold all probabilities ≥0.5 as present and <0.5 as absent for these metrics

Presence accuracy
The fraction of examples where the correct species observed at a location was predicted as present. This is “zero-one accuracy” in the deepbiosphere code.



Comparing uniform train-test split for bee flowers (left) and full dataset (right) for the two states (rows)




Precision score
Precision Measures how many species predicted to be present were actually present.



Comparing uniform train-test split for bee flowers (left) and full dataset (right) for the two states (rows)




Recall score
Recall Measures how many of the true species present are predicted as present.



Comparing uniform train-test split for bee flowers (left) and full dataset (right) for the two states (rows)




F1 score
F1 score The harmonic mean of precision and recall and represents a conservative mean of the two (i.e. is more affected by low values).



Comparing uniform train-test split for bee flowers (left) and full dataset (right) for the two states (rows)

title: Accuracy metrics – uniform train-test
text:
Discrimination metrics
In order to take into account the effect of thresholds, discrimination metrics measure binary classification ability across a wide range of thresholds in order to calculate an SDM’s performance across a wide range of presence thresholds and describe the relationship between threshold change and performance change.

Area under curve [ROC] – uncalibrated
AUC ROC Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve averaged across species



Comparing uniform train-test split for bee flowers (left) and full dataset (right) for the two states (rows)




Area under curve [PRC] – uncalibrated
AUC PRC Average area under the precision-recall curve averaged across species



Comparing uniform train-test split for bee flowers (left) and full dataset (right) for the two states (rows)




Calibrated area under curves
A model which has extremely low predicted probabilities can still nevertheless have a high AUCROC if within its range of predicted probabilities said model has good sensitivity and specificity for that class.

This means that it’s possible to have a model that never predicts a species as present with the standard presence/absence threshold of 0.5 yet still has a high average AUCROC.
To correct for this, we also introduce a calibrated area under the curve score where the chosen thresholds are linearly interpolated values between 0 and 1.


Calibrated AUC [ROC]



Comparing uniform train-test split for bee flowers (left) and full dataset (right) for the two states (rows)




Calibrated AUC [PRC]



Comparing uniform train-test split for bee flowers (left) and full dataset (right) for the two states (rows)

Top-K (top 1, 5, 30, 100) These metrics measure how many times the correct species was correctly predicted within the top-K highest-ranked species within a given image (where, for example, K=5 would be the 5 species with the highest probability of presence).

I also thinned the dataset of records that expressly included flowering, though these were already less redundant. The thinned flowering distribution is shown in blue, while the original dataset is shown in orange.

title: Accuracy metrics – spatial cross-validation
text: These are the results from conducting spatial cross validation. Because of the shapes of Pennsylvania and New York, I used 10 bands running North-South across these states as the test bands for 10-fold cross validation. Below I show the distributions for the overall model metrics for PA and NY. Significance comparisons are made between the cross-validation accuracy metrics of deepbiosphere and two conventional modeling approaches: Maxent trained on bioclimatic data and random forest trained on bioclimatic data.

title: Phenology
text:
Using rgbif, I searched for all research-grade observations of the top 100 floral resource plants across PA and NY within the NE US from 2016-2020. I matched these reports by location and week to growing degree day, estimated from 4-km PRISM data based on Sarah Goslee’s past work. Then I fit finite mixture models to these distributions, using the mixtools R package.
Data from GBIF includes occasional information on plant reproductive stage, if it was available from the observation. I added this in these plots to provide some reference for the finite mixture model predictions, in orange.

Comparing the finite mixture model distributions to the flowering records distribution, I can guess that the first distribution (dist = 1) corresponds with flowering.















Animation of growing degree days in PA





# use distribution 1
cc.d <- 1

cc.mu <- cc.mix$mu[cc.d]
cc.sigma <- cc.mix$sigma[cc.d]

pa_gdd <- rast("data-raw/big/pa_gdd2017_256m.tif")

# apply pnorm function to stack of gdd rasters
pa_gdd_cdf <- terra::app(pa_gdd, pnorm, mean = cc.mu, sd = cc.sigma)

# add a 0 raster at the beginning of the gdd time series to substract from
pa_gdd_0 <- pa_gdd[[1]]*0
pa_gdd_0cdf <- c(pa_gdd_0, pa_gdd_cdf)

# find difference in cumulative probability between weeks
pa_bloompb <- terra::diff(pa_gdd_0cdf, filename = "data-raw/big/CCanadensis_bpb.tif")




Animation of Cercis canadensis bloom probability in PA





Multiply species distribution with gdd-based bloom probability

cc_stbp <- cc_flrpb * ccdf




Animation of C. canadensis spatiotemporal bloom occurence probability
